# walker-lane-tactics-jiean-yin

**Lane Tactics · Jiean Yin · current layer: Assignment 3 — Your First 3D Game Assets with Claude, the Blender MCP, and Blender**

*Lane Tactics* (working title): a turn-based, simultaneous-orders tactics game. Carved wooden pieces fight on a five-lane tabletop board, and you win by standing a piece on the enemy's back row. This is the one game I build all semester: each assignment adds a layer to this repository and is submitted as a git tag (`a3` for Assignment 3).

**Started from:** an empty Godot 4.7.2 project (no code from walker-jumpman or my Assignment 1). The test-and-evidence practice and document set come from Assignment 1, which extended Nik Bear Brown's [walker-jumpman](https://github.com/nikbearbrown/walker-jumpman). See [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md).

| Tool | Version |
|---|---|
| Godot | 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf, standard build (not .NET), Compatibility renderer |
| Blender | 5.2.2 LTS (the course chapter used 5.1.2); glTF 2.0 exporter 5.2.40 |
| Blender MCP | [mcp-for-blender](https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender) 2.1.9 (server, from PyPI) with its Blender add-on 1.8; uv 0.13.1; telemetry off; every asset library and generator off |
| Claude Code | 2.1.295 (bundled with the Claude desktop app), Claude Opus 5.5 |
| OS | Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200 |

## Game Design Document

[GDD.md](GDD.md) is the whole game in one document: concept, game flow, assets, characters, the story told episode by episode, gameplay (goal, mechanics, abilities, the four episodes, losing and restarting, player skills), graphics, sound and the technical description. It brings together the design docs below and adds the campaign: goblin enemies, mountains, night raids, the Mend ability and the giant boss. The rules for all of this are in [RULES.md](RULES.md), and how each one was decided is in [DESIGN-HISTORY.md](DESIGN-HISTORY.md) section 8. The figures come from `design/tools/draw_gdd_sketches.py` (rendered with `bash design/tools/render_png.sh design/gdd`).

## Assignment 3 — three 3D assets in a Godot diorama

Lane Tactics is 2D, so this assignment adds a small **3D tabletop diorama** (`godot/diorama/asset_diorama.tscn`: a floor, one light, a camera) with three low-poly assets that I directed Claude to build in my running Blender through the MCP. Later assignments reuse this scene; it is not connected to the 2D game yet.

| Asset | What it is in the game | Size W × D × H (m) | Triangles / budget | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `archer_piece` | the carved wooden archer unit, in player teal | 0.40 × 0.40 × 0.80 | 254 / 400 | [blend](blender/archer_piece.blend) · [build code](tools/blender/build_archer_piece.py) · [glb](godot/assets/models/archer_piece.glb) |
| `board_square` | one linen square of the 5-lane board | 1.00 × 1.00 × 0.05 | 60 / 100 | [blend](blender/board_square.blend) · [build code](tools/blender/build_board_square.py) · [glb](godot/assets/models/board_square.glb) |
| `goal_flag` | marks the enemy back row you must reach | 0.45 × 0.30 × 1.20 | 84 / 150 | [blend](blender/goal_flag.blend) · [build code](tools/blender/build_goal_flag.py) · [glb](godot/assets/models/goal_flag.glb) |

Scale: **1 board square = 1 m**, and 1 Blender unit = 1 Godot unit = 1 m, so nothing is converted. Every origin is the centre of the asset's underside; every transform is applied (scale 1, 1, 1).

**What this layer added**

- [CHANGE-BRIEF.md](CHANGE-BRIEF.md) Assignment 3 section: sizes, origins, colours, budgets and six predicted failures, committed before any build (`78b213f`), plus revision A3-R1 (darker board border).
- All three assets built through the MCP route (every `execute_blender_code` body is in `tools/blender/build_<asset>.py`); one hand edit of mine in Blender's window (the archer's bow moved 0.08 m so it no longer hides the eye).
- Export to `.glb` with headless Blender from the committed `.blend` files: [tools/blender/export_glb.py](tools/blender/export_glb.py) (+Y Up; refuses an object whose transforms are not applied).
- The diorama scene and a headless check, [godot/tests/check_assets.gd](godot/tests/check_assets.gd), which prints each asset's bounding box, node scale, up axis, lowest point, triangle count and material colours, and checks that each sits on the diorama floor inside the camera's view.
- Records: [BLENDER-NOTES.md](BLENDER-NOTES.md) (the interface in my own words), [TEST-REPORT.md](TEST-REPORT.md) (Assignment 3 section), [FRICTIONAL.md](FRICTIONAL.md) (Assignment 3 section), [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md).

**Run the check and open the scene** (Windows, Git Bash; on macOS use your Godot path and Homebrew's `timeout`)

```bash
timeout 300 <Godot console exe> --headless --path godot --import
timeout 120 <Godot console exe> --headless --path godot --script res://tests/check_assets.gd --fixed-fps 60
<Godot exe> --path godot res://diorama/asset_diorama.tscn
```

The check exits 0 when every assertion passes and writes `evidence/check_assets-<timestamp>.json` (last run: **38/38**, [evidence/check_assets-1792106192.json](evidence/check_assets-1792106192.json)). In the editor: **Import** `godot/project.godot`, open `res://diorama/asset_diorama.tscn`, press **F6** to see it through the camera. The 2D slice is still the project's main scene (F5).

Re-export (only needed after changing a `.blend`): `<Blender exe> -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python tools/blender/export_glb.py -- blender godot/assets/models`

**What the check does not show:** that anything renders or looks right (headless Godot uses a dummy renderer), how the colours read under the lamp, or whether the shapes read as an archer, a square and a flag. That is the human look check in TEST-REPORT A3.5.

**Known limitations (Assignment 3)**

- The goal flag is a 2 cm box: seen exactly from the side (±X) it is edge-on and nearly disappears. The archer's bow is a straight box and reads more like a staff.
- Claude counted the triangles from the mesh; my Blender Scene Statistics cross-check is in TEST-REPORT A3.3.
- The diorama `.tscn` was written by Claude as text and is not connected to the 2D game.
- One computer (Windows only) and one tester.

### Film (Assignment 3)

**"Lane Tactics in 3D: A Piece, a Square, a Goal"**, the Brutalist `godot-gamedev walker` explainer, 4:41, 3840 × 2160, 30 fps, narrated by Liam (local Kokoro TTS).

| | |
|---|---|
| Link | [https://youtu.be/Cb2F8_0mYhk](https://youtu.be/Cb2F8_0mYhk) (YouTube, channel @JieanYin; video title "3D Game Assets with Claude, the Blender MCP, and Blender") |
| File | `claude-liam-walker-lane-tactics-jiean-yin-a3-gamedev.mp4` (kept out of GitHub; MP4) |
| SHA-256 | `83d2489e2ee1f6e6c2d5ffc1df5387f086fba0c51a983904e08b93a2d4ad4240` |
| Game source shown | commit `e415255` (`godot/` identical to the submitted tag `a3`) |

It uses my own screen recordings (the archer after Claude's build, my hand edit, and the Claude window when I approved the flag build), my own Godot screenshot, and a new Movie Maker capture of the real diorama scene with a scripted camera. Claude's archer build and any Blender view of the flag build are not in my recordings; the film says so and does not reconstruct them. Beat sheet, script, prompts, capture records and QC: [youtube/claude-liam-walker-lane-tactics-jiean-yin-a3-gamedev/](youtube/claude-liam-walker-lane-tactics-jiean-yin-a3-gamedev/).

## Assignment 2 — the 2D asset slice

The **asset slice** is a small playable scene that proves the generated art, sound effects and music work together.

![The slice: your archer draws on the enemy archer (engine screenshot, scripted input)](evidence/screens-1791864538/09-attack-hit-enemy-hurt.png)

### Run it

Requires the standard **Godot 4.7.2** build (not .NET).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jiean-Yin/walker-lane-tactics-jiean-yin.git
cd walker-lane-tactics-jiean-yin
```

- **Windows:** clone into a folder whose path is shorter than about 120 characters (for example inside `Downloads`). The longest file path in the repository is 134 characters, and Windows rejects full paths over 260 unless `git config --global core.longpaths true` is set.
- **Editor:** open Godot, **Import**, choose `godot/project.godot`, press **Run** (F5).
- **Command line:** `<Godot exe> --path godot`
- **Tests** (headless, each writes a timestamped report to `evidence/`):

  ```bash
  <Godot console exe> --headless --path godot --import
  <Godot console exe> --headless --path godot --script res://tests/test_rules.gd
  <Godot console exe> --headless --path godot --script res://tests/test_audio_events.gd
  ```

### Controls

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter | start; confirm the order; play again |
| Arrows / WASD | move phase: choose a neighbouring square · attack phase: cycle the valid targets |
| Space | stay (move) or hold fire (attack) |
| R | retry from turn 1 |
| P / Esc | pause and unpause (music gets quieter) |
| **M** | mute and unmute **music** |
| **N** | mute and unmute **sound effects** |
| F3 | show the footprint slots (debug, display only) |

Your teal archer starts in your back row (left). One red enemy archer marches toward it. Each turn you step, then shoot any square within two steps that holds an enemy. Who strikes first alternates every turn, as the HUD shows. Win by defeating the enemy or by standing on the red back row.

### What the slice demonstrates

| | What | Made with |
|---|---|---|
| Character | the archer swaps one static image per state: **idle, draw, hurt, defeat, win**. It faces right, and the enemy is the same art recoloured and flipped. Art is anchored on the base disc inside a per-square footprint | Stable Diffusion XL base 1.0, run locally (seeds in [assets/gen-log.jsonl](assets/gen-log.jsonl)) |
| Environment | warm-lit walnut tabletop behind the code-drawn linen board | SDXL base 1.0 |
| Sound effects | **SFX-HOP** (a piece lands), **SFX-HIT** (your arrow lands), **SFX-HURT** (you are hit), **SFX-WIN** (you win), each fired once per event from the rules engine's event list | ElevenLabs Sound Effects (free plan) |
| Music | a 24-second, 8-bar loop that plays on the title and in play, ducks on pause, fades out on defeat, stops on win, and restarts on retry | MusicGen small, run locally |

The design came first, committed before any generation: [CONCEPT.md](CONCEPT.md) · [STORYBOARD.md](STORYBOARD.md) · [CHARACTER-SHEET.md](CHARACTER-SHEET.md) · [CHANGE-BRIEF.md](CHANGE-BRIEF.md) · [RULES.md](RULES.md). The rest of the record: [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md) (models, licences, the asset log with every rejected output) · [TEST-REPORT.md](TEST-REPORT.md) · [FRICTIONAL.md](FRICTIONAL.md). Rejected outputs are in [assets/rejected/](assets/rejected/).

### Known limitations

- **Muted play:** the red target marker is hard to see on a square that holds a piece, and a new player cannot tell why the enemy moves or stops (author's playtest). Planned next: a clearer target colour and a simpler enemy that keeps moving toward the end and avoids direct contact.
- The slice uses **one enemy**; the storyboard drew two. With two, the search showed it could only be won on the tie rule (CHANGE-BRIEF R1).
- **Pose mismatches** against the sheet: hurt has no squint; defeat has a dot eye and a navy bow; the arms cover the face in the win pose. The idle base disc is redrawn by hand.
- The ElevenLabs sounds have no seed, and the exact game description added to their prompts was not recorded.
- One human tester (the author); Windows only.

### Film

**"Lane Tactics: From Sketch to Seed to Sound"**, the Brutalist `godot-gamedev walker` explainer, 6:08, 3840 × 2160, 30 fps, narrated by Liam (local Kokoro TTS).

   114			var k: float = _hop_t / _hop_dur
   115			position = _hop_from.lerp(_hop_to, k)
   116			_set_lift(HOP_HEIGHT * sin(PI * k))
   117		if _hurt_left > 0.0:
   118			_hurt_left -= dt
   119			if _hurt_left <= 0.0 and state == "hurt":
   120				set_state("idle")
   121		if _recover_left > 0.0:

   123			if _recover_left <= 0.0 and state == "recover":
   124				set_state("idle")

   141			tex = _load_tex(ART_DIR + "archer_%s.png" % state_name)
   142			if tex != null:

   144		else:

   152		if _tex_cache.has(path):
   153			return _tex_cache[path]
   154		var tex: Texture2D = null
   155		if ResourceLoader.exists(path):
   156			var res: Resource = load(path)
   157			if res is Texture2D:
   158				tex = res as Texture2D
   159		_tex_cache[path] = tex

   164		if _sprite == null:
   165			return
   166		var found: Array = _find_texture(state)
   167		if found[0] == null and OPTIONAL_FALLBACK.has(state):

   170		texture_source = found[1]

   174			return

   176		var ref: Texture2D = _find_texture("idle")[0]

   178			ref = tex

   180		_sprite.texture = tex
   181		_sprite.visible = true

   183		_sprite.scale = Vector2(s, s)
   184		_sprite.flip_h = facing < 0
   185		_sprite.position = Vector2(0.0, -tex.get_height() * s * 0.5 + BASE_FROM_BOTTOM - _lift)

   223				draw_arc(Vector2(18.0, -78.0), 10.0, -2.6, 0.6, 12, COL_WALNUT, 3.0)

   225				draw_arc(Vector2(4.0, -32.0), 20.0, -1.2, 1.2, 16, COL_WALNUT, 3.5)
   226				draw_line(Vector2(11.2, -50.6), Vector2(11.2, -13.4), COL_INK, 1.2)
   227		# state label, unflipped, so the placeholder is obviously a placeholder
   228		draw_set_transform(Vector2(0.0, -_lift), 0.0, Vector2.ONE)
   229		var font: Font = ThemeDB.fallback_font
   230		var label: String = "[%s]" % state

52		"lt_retry", "lt_pause", "lt_music", "lt_sfx", "lt_debug"]

56		"lt_right": [KEY_RIGHT, KEY_D],
57		"lt_up": [KEY_UP, KEY_W],

62		"lt_music": [KEY_M],

66	const DIRS: Dictionary = {
67		"lt_left": Vector2i(-1, 0), "lt_right": Vector2i(1, 0), "lt_up": Vector2i(0, -1), "lt_down": Vector2i(0, 1),
68	}

70	static var _tex_cache: Dictionary = {}
71	
72	## Playback speed multiplier (tests use it to run fast). Never changes rules.
73	var time_scale: float = 1.0
74	var rules: RulesScript
75	var audio: AudioDirectorScript
76	var state: State = State.TITLE
77	var paused: bool = false
78	var debug_footprints: bool = false
79	var show_results: bool = false
80	var retries: int = 0
81	var event_log: Array[Dictionary] = [] ## every rules event of this session
82	var played_events: Array[Dictionary] = [] ## events whose moment has been shown by playback
83	var ignored_inputs: int = 0
84	var ignored_echoes: int = 0

87	var legal_cells: Array[Vector2i] = []
88	var targets: Array[Vector2i] = []
89	var target_index: int = -1
90	var has_marked_target: bool = false
91	var marked_target: Vector2i = Vector2i.ZERO
92	var display_hp: Dictionary = {}
93	var pieces: Dictionary = {} ## unit id -> piece
94

96	var _pieces_root: Node2D
97	var _fx_layer: Node2D
98	var _hud_layer: Node2D
99	var _cues: Array[Dictionary] = []
100	var _clock: float = 0.0

102	var _arrows: Array[Dictionary] = []
103	var _message: String = ""

109	func _ready() -> void:
110		_ensure_actions()
111		rules = RulesScript.new()
112		audio = get_node_or_null("AudioDirector") as AudioDirectorScript
113		if audio == null:
114			audio = AudioDirectorScript.new()

131	func _make_layer(fn: Callable, z: int) -> Node2D:
132		var n: Node2D = DrawLayerScript.new()
133		n.draw_fn = fn
134		n.z_index = z
135		add_child(n)

138	
139	static func _ensure_actions() -> void:
140		for action: String in ACTION_ORDER:
141			if InputMap.has_action(action):
142				continue
143			InputMap.add_action(action)
144			for code: int in ACTION_KEYS[action]:
145				var ev: InputEventKey = InputEventKey.new()
146				ev.physical_keycode = code as Key
147				InputMap.action_add_event(action, ev)

150	func state_name() -> String:
151		return STATE_NAMES[state]
152	
153	
154	func selected_target() -> Variant:
155		if target_index >= 0 and target_index < targets.size():
156			return targets[target_index]
157		return null

159	
160	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- clock
161	
162	func _process(delta: float) -> void:
163		var dt: float = delta * time_scale
164		audio.time_scale = time_scale
165		_time += delta
166		if not paused:
167			_clock += dt
168			_run_cues()
169			for p: PieceScript in pieces.values():
170				p.tick(dt)
171			_tick_fx(dt)
172			if _message_left > 0.0:
173				_message_left -= dt
174			if _card_lock > 0.0:
175				_card_lock -= dt
176		_board_layer.queue_redraw()
177		_fx_layer.queue_redraw()
178		_hud_layer.queue_redraw()
179	
180	
181	func _schedule(t: float, fn: Callable) -> void:
182		var i: int = _cues.size()
183		while i > 0 and float(_cues[i - 1]["t"]) > t:
184			i -= 1
185		_cues.insert(i, {"t": t, "fn": fn})
186	
187	
188	func _clear_cues() -> void:
189		_cues.clear()
190		_clock = 0.0
191	
192	
193	func _run_cues() -> void:
194		while not _cues.is_empty() and float(_cues[0]["t"]) <= _clock:
195			var c: Dictionary = _cues.pop_front()
196			(c["fn"] as Callable).call()
197	
198	
199	func _tick_fx(dt: float) -> void:
200		for f: Dictionary in _floaters:
201			f["t"] = float(f["t"]) + dt
202		_floaters = _floaters.filter(func(f: Dictionary) -> bool: return float(f["t"]) < FLOAT_TIME)
203		for a: Dictionary in _arrows:
204			a["t"] = float(a["t"]) + dt
205		_arrows = _arrows.filter(func(a: Dictionary) -> bool: return float(a["t"]) < ARROW_TIME)
206	
207	
208	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- input
209	
210	func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
211		if not (event is InputEventKey):
212			return
213		var k: InputEventKey = event as InputEventKey
214		if not k.pressed:
215			return
216		if k.is_echo():
217			ignored_echoes += 1 # held keys never act
218			get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
219			return
220		var action: String = _action_for(k)
221		if action == "":
222			return
223		get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()
224		_handle_action(action, k)
225	
226	
227	func _action_for(event: InputEvent) -> String:
228		for action: String in ACTION_ORDER:
229			if event.is_action(action):
230				return action
231		return ""
232	
233	
234	func _handle_action(action: String, k: InputEventKey) -> void:
235		match action:
236			"lt_music":
237				audio.toggle_music_mute()
238				return
239			"lt_sfx":
240				audio.toggle_sfx_mute()
241				return
242			"lt_debug":
243				debug_footprints = not debug_footprints
244				return
245		if state == State.TITLE:
246			if action == "lt_confirm":
247				_start_play()
248			else:
249				ignored_inputs += 1
250			return
251		if action == "lt_pause":
252			if _in_play():
253				_set_paused(not paused)
254			elif show_results and (k.keycode == KEY_ESCAPE or k.physical_keycode == KEY_ESCAPE):
255				get_tree().quit()
256			else:
257				ignored_inputs += 1
258			return
259		if paused:
260			ignored_inputs += 1
261			return
262		if action == "lt_retry":
263			_restart(true)
264			return
265		match state:
266			State.PLAN_MOVE:
267				if DIRS.has(action):
268					_adjust_move(DIRS[action])
269				elif action == "lt_confirm":
270					_confirm_move(planned_offset)
271				elif action == "lt_stay":
272					_confirm_move(Vector2i.ZERO)
273			State.PLAN_ATTACK:
274				if action == "lt_left" or action == "lt_up":
275					_cycle_target(-1)
276				elif action == "lt_right" or action == "lt_down":
277					_cycle_target(1)
278				elif action == "lt_confirm":
279					_confirm_attack(selected_target())
280				elif action == "lt_stay":
281					_confirm_attack(null)
282			State.WON, State.LOST:
283				if action != "lt_confirm" or _card_lock > 0.0:
284					ignored_inputs += 1
285				elif not show_results:
286					show_results = true
287				else:
288					_restart(false)
289			_:
290				ignored_inputs += 1 # playback: gameplay input is ignored
291	
292	
293	func _in_play() -> bool:
294		return state in [State.PLAN_MOVE, State.PLAY_MOVES, State.PLAN_ATTACK, State.PLAY_ATTACKS]
295	
296	
297	func _set_paused(p: bool) -> void:
298		paused = p
299		audio.set_paused(p)
300	
301	
302	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- session
303	
304	func _start_play() -> void:
305		rules.reset()
306		event_log.clear()
307		played_events.clear()
308		_build_pieces()
309		_begin_plan_move()
310	
311	
312	## Retry (R) or play again (Enter on results): full reset to turn 1, music from the top.
313	func _restart(is_retry: bool) -> void:
314		if is_retry:
315			retries += 1
316		else:
317			retries = 0
318		_clear_cues()
319		_arrows.clear()
320		_floaters.clear()
321		_set_paused(false)
322		show_results = false
323		has_marked_target = false
324		_message_left = 0.0
325		last_result = {}
326		rules.reset()
327		event_log.clear()
328		played_events.clear()
329		_build_pieces()
330		for p: PieceScript in pieces.values():
331			p.show_recover()
332		audio.new_session()
333		_begin_plan_move()
334	
335	
336	func _build_pieces() -> void:
337		for p: Node in _pieces_root.get_children():
338			p.queue_free()
339			_pieces_root.remove_child(p)
340		pieces.clear()
341		display_hp.clear()
342		var cells: Dictionary = {}
343		for u: Dictionary in rules.units:
344			cells[u["id"]] = RulesScript.cell_of(u)
345		for u: Dictionary in rules.units:
346			var p: PieceScript = PieceScript.new()
347			p.name = String(u["id"])
348			_pieces_root.add_child(p)
349			p.setup(u["id"], u["team"], int(u["facing"]), RulesScript.cell_of(u))
350			p.position = _slot_pos(u["id"], cells)
351			pieces[u["id"]] = p
352			display_hp[u["id"]] = int(u["hp"])
353	
354	
355	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- move phase
356	
357	func _begin_plan_move() -> void:
358		state = State.PLAN_MOVE
359		planned_offset = Vector2i.ZERO
360		legal_cells = rules.legal_moves(PLAYER_ID)
361		targets.clear()
362		target_index = -1
363	
364	
365	func _adjust_move(d: Vector2i) -> void:
366		var nxt: Vector2i = Vector2i(clampi(planned_offset.x + d.x, -1, 1), clampi(planned_offset.y + d.y, -1, 1))
367		var here: Vector2i = RulesScript.cell_of(rules.get_unit(PLAYER_ID))
368		if RulesScript.on_board(here + nxt):
369			planned_offset = nxt
370	
371	
372	func _confirm_move(offset: Vector2i) -> void:
373		_message_left = 0.0 # a transient message lasts until the next decision
374		var events: Array[Dictionary] = rules.resolve_moves({PLAYER_ID: offset})
375		event_log.append_array(events)
376		_play_moves(events)
377	
378	
379	func _play_moves(events: Array[Dictionary]) -> void:
380		_clear_cues()
381		state = State.PLAY_MOVES
382		var final_cells: Dictionary = {}
383		for id: String in pieces:
384			final_cells[id] = (pieces[id] as PieceScript).cell
385		for ev: Dictionary in events:
386			final_cells[ev["unit"]] = ev["to"]
387		var i: int = 0
388		for ev: Dictionary in events:
389			var start: float = HOP_STAGGER * i
390			_schedule(start, _cue_hop_start.bind(ev, final_cells))
391			_schedule(start + HOP_TIME, _cue_hop_land.bind(ev))
392			i += 1
393		var end: float = (HOP_STAGGER * (i - 1) + HOP_TIME if i > 0 else 0.0) + MOVE_TAIL
394		_schedule(end, _after_moves)
395	
396	
397	func _cue_hop_start(ev: Dictionary, final_cells: Dictionary) -> void:
398		var p: PieceScript = pieces[ev["unit"]]
399		var from: Vector2i = ev["from"]
400		var to: Vector2i = ev["to"]
401		if to.x != from.x:
402			p.set_facing(1 if to.x > from.x else -1)
403		p.start_hop(p.position, _slot_pos(ev["unit"], final_cells), HOP_TIME)
404	
405	
406	func _cue_hop_land(ev: Dictionary) -> void:
407		var p: PieceScript = pieces[ev["unit"]]
408		p.cell = ev["to"]

576	## Base-disc position for a unit given everyone's cells: one unit centred, two in left/right slots.
577	func _slot_pos(id: String, cells: Dictionary) -> Vector2:
578		var c: Vector2i = cells[id]
579		var group: Array[String] = []
580		for other: String in cells:
581			if cells[other] == c:
582				group.append(other)
583		group.sort_custom(func(a: String, b: String) -> bool:
584			var ta: int = 0 if _team_of(a) == RulesScript.PLAYER else 1
585			var tb: int = 0 if _team_of(b) == RulesScript.PLAYER else 1
586			if ta != tb:
587				return ta < tb
588			return a < b)
589		var n: int = group.size()
590		var i: int = group.find(id)
591		var off: float = 0.0
592		if n == 2:
593			off = -SLOT_OFFSET if i == 0 else SLOT_OFFSET
594		elif n > 2:
595			off = lerpf(-40.0, 40.0, float(i) / float(n - 1))
596		var r: Rect2 = _cell_rect(c)
597		return Vector2(r.position.x + SQUARE.x * 0.5 + off, r.position.y + BASE_Y)

@AGENTS.md

# Project context

Every fact below has a file reference. Line numbers are from commit `5a32988`.

- **Engine:** Godot 4.7 (`godot/project.godot:9`, `config/features` "4.7"); the exact build, 4.7.2 standard (not .NET), is recorded in `README.md` (tool table) and `AGENTS.md`.
- **Renderer:** Compatibility, `renderer/rendering_method="gl_compatibility"` (`godot/project.godot:24`, mobile also Compatibility at `:25`). HDR 2D is not set in `project.godot`. Default 2D texture filter is set to 1 (`project.godot:23`).
- **Main scene:** `res://game/main.tscn` (`godot/project.godot:7`): a `Node2D` running `godot/game/main.gd` plus an `AudioDirector` node (`godot/game/main.tscn:6-10`). Viewport 1280 × 720, stretch `canvas_items` (`project.godot:15-18`).
- **3D scene:** `godot/diorama/asset_diorama.tscn`, not connected to the 2D game (`README.md`, A3 section).

## The object the `exposed` tint shades (2D)

- The player archer is a `piece.gd` node (`godot/game/piece.gd`), built by `main._build_pieces()` (`godot/game/main.gd:336-352`) under the y-sorted `Pieces` root (`main.gd:119-123`). Pieces are freed and rebuilt on start (`main.gd:308`) and on retry / play again (`main.gd:329`).
- It is drawn by one `Sprite2D` child, `_sprite` (`piece.gd:35`), created once in `setup()` (`piece.gd:51-54`). `_apply_visual()` (`piece.gd:163-186`) swaps its `texture` per pose, sets `modulate`, `scale`, `flip_h` and `position`. No material is set anywhere today.
- Textures: `res://assets/art/archer_<state>.png` for the player, `archer_<state>_enemy.png` for the enemy (`piece.gd:4-6`, `:135-148`); `archer_idle_enemy.png` exists, so the enemy idle has `modulate` white. Only if an enemy image is missing does it fall back to the player image with `ENEMY_TINT` in `modulate` (`piece.gd:17`, `:141-143`).
- Without any image the piece draws a code placeholder in `_draw()` and hides the sprite (`piece.gd:170-173`, `:191-233`); a material on the sprite would not shade that.
- The pieces' own clock: `tick(dt)` is called by main with scaled time and not while paused (`piece.gd:110-111`, `main.gd:162-171`).

## The game state that drives the effect

- Owner: `godot/game/main.gd`. Fields: `state` (`main.gd:76`, enum at `:13`), `planned_offset` (`main.gd:86`), `paused` (`main.gd:77`, set only in `_set_paused()` `:297-299`), `time_scale` (`main.gd:73`). `PLAYER_ID` is `"p1"` (`main.gd:17`); `pieces` maps unit id → piece (`main.gd:93`).
- PLAN_MOVE begins in `_begin_plan_move()` (`main.gd:357-362`, resets `planned_offset` to zero); arrows change it via `_adjust_move()` (`main.gd:365-369`); Enter / Space leave it via `_confirm_move()` → `PLAY_MOVES` (`main.gd:372-381`); R calls `_restart(true)` (`main.gd:262-263`, `:313-333`).
- Game time: `dt = delta * time_scale`, advanced only when `not paused` (`main.gd:162-171`). The game never uses `get_tree().paused` (`main.gd:6`).
- Unit cells live in `rules.units` (`godot/game/rules.gd:29`); read with `RulesScript.cell_of()` and `rules.get_unit()`, liveness with `rules.is_alive()` (used at `main.gd:656`). Reach: `Rules.in_range()` (`rules.gd:120-123`, Chebyshev 1..2).
- Target red `COL_TARGET = #E0453A` (`main.gd:47`); board squares `#D8C7A0` / `#CDB98E` (`main.gd:41-42`).

## The 3D object for the textured shader

- Scene: `godot/diorama/asset_diorama.tscn`. Today it holds `WorldEnvironment` (ambient colour light, energy 0.35, `:15-25`), a 5 × 3 m `Floor` `PlaneMesh` with an inline `StandardMaterial3D` (`:7-13`, `:27-28`), one `DirectionalLight3D` `Lamp` with shadows (`:30-33`), `Camera3D` at (0, 1.1, 3), fov 50 (`:35-39`), and the three A3 `.glb` instances (`:41-47`).
- The brief's objects, `LinenSquareLight` and `LinenSquareDark` (`MeshInstance3D` + 1 m `PlaneMesh`), **do not exist yet**; the A3 `board_square.glb` is not used because it has no UVs (`CHANGE-BRIEF.md` §4).
- Material source (planned, per `CHANGE-BRIEF.md` §4): `ShaderMaterial` files `godot/materials/linen_light.tres` and `linen_dark.tres` using `godot/shaders/linen_square.gdshader`, with textures from `godot/assets/textures/hessian_380/` (files present; credits in `ATTRIBUTION.md` there).
- `godot/tests/check_assets.gd` loads this scene (`:168`) and requires exactly one `Light3D` (`:183-187`).

## Test commands (all through `scripts/run-test.sh`)

The wrapper (`scripts/run-test.sh`) takes `<test-file.gd> <fps>`, runs `${GODOT:-godot} --headless --path godot --script res://tests/<file> --fixed-fps <fps>` under `timeout 120`, tees to `logs/<name>_<fps>fps.log`, and fails if the log contains `SHADER ERROR` or `SCRIPT ERROR`. Set `GODOT` to the console build. Run from the repository root:

```bash
./scripts/run-test.sh test_rules.gd 60         # rules engine, 51/51 at baseline
./scripts/run-test.sh test_audio_events.gd 60  # main.tscn driven by key presses, 70/70
./scripts/run-test.sh check_assets.gd 60       # A3 diorama assets, 38/38
```

Baseline counts and the two known non-failing `ERROR` lines are in commit `eb1ff2a` and `evidence/a5/baseline/`. Each suite also writes `evidence/<name>-<unix time>.json` (`godot/tests/test_report.gd:2`, `:34`). Before the first run, and after adding textures or shaders, import once (not a test, so not through the wrapper; `README.md` A3 section): `"$GODOT" --headless --path godot --import`. Clean saved logs with `scripts/redact-paths.sh` before committing them.

Not wrapper suites: `godot/tests/capture.gd` needs a real renderer (`capture.gd:2-3`), and `analyze_variants.gd` is analysis (`analyze_variants.gd:2`). `route_runner.gd` and `test_report.gd` are helpers.

# Current change

@CHANGE-BRIEF.md

# Ownership

Files in `godot/shaders/` are hand-written by the human (Jiean) and are never edited by an agent: not created, not changed, not "fixed", not reformatted. That includes `exposed_tint.gdshader`, `linen_square.gdshader` and `hint_experiment.gdshader`. If a shader looks wrong, report it with the evidence and stop.

# Out of scope

- Game rules and state: `godot/game/rules.gd`, the `State` machine, every timing constant and transition in `main.gd`, and how input is handled. No new key. The driver reads `state`, `planned_offset`, `paused`, `time_scale` and unit cells; it never writes them.
- Everything the player sees apart from the archer sprite's tint: the board drawing, markers, HUD, cards, effects, the enemy piece's look, sounds and music.
- Existing tests and their expected counts (`test_rules`, `test_audio_events`, `check_assets`): new checks go in new test files.
- Every A2 and A3 asset file: the art PNGs, sounds, music, the `.glb` models, `.blend` files and Blender scripts. No importer material on `board_square.glb`; the existing diorama nodes, lamp, environment and camera stay as they are (only the two new tiles are added).
- Engine and project settings: renderer, HDR 2D, stretch, filters in `project.godot`.
- No use of `TIME` in the tint; no shared `ShaderMaterial` across pieces; the DirectX normal map is never bound.

# Unconfirmed

1. The exact Godot build (4.7.2) is only in `README.md`/`AGENTS.md`; `project.godot` says "4.7". Not run in this step.
2. `godot/shaders/`, `godot/materials/`, the two linen tiles, `hint_greys.png` and the script that writes it, and the A5 test files do not exist yet; their names and the commands that will run them are not known. They should go through the wrapper at 30, 60 and 144 fps (`CHANGE-BRIEF.md` R2).
3. The Hessian 380 textures have no `.import` files yet, so the import settings in `CHANGE-BRIEF.md` §4 (lossless, normal-map flag, mipmaps) are not in place and were not checked.
4. Where the driver will live (in `main.gd`, in `piece.gd`, or a new node) is not decided in the files. A new driver means editing a game script, which this step did not do; the brief allows presentation code that only reads state.
5. Whether `_apply_visual()` resetting the sprite each pose change would interact with a material was not checked; nothing in `piece.gd` sets or clears `material` today.
6. The brief's pixel predictions (P1, P2 screen positions) and the Compatibility-renderer behaviour of `source_color` were not re-measured here.
7. The import command is taken from `README.md`; `scripts/run-test.sh` has no import mode.
